chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And remember your Lord when you forget'. He said: 'That is regarding the oath, when you say, 'By Allah, I will not do such and such'. So when you remember that you did not make an exclusion, then say, 'If Allah wills'.'
ai.seo_question: How to fulfill the Quranic command to 'remember your Lord when you forget' in the context of oaths?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Quranic command to 'remember your Lord when you forget' specifically applies to the context of oaths, instructing that if one swears without the condition 'Insha'Allah' and later recalls the omission, they must utter it to validate the oath. This interpretation highlights the practical application of the verse in daily speech, ensuring that human actions remain subject to divine will and preventing the oath from becoming absolute. The ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating Quranic principles into the minutiae of legal and social conduct.
